# @zakkster/lite-di-event-bus

> DI-constructed static event handlers under a boot-locked `multi` topology,
> dispatched by index over one bus-owned buffer. Listeners are classes the
> container builds and owns; emit routes through the container so it fails closed
> after shutdown. Synchronous emit allocates 0 bytes/emit (hard-gated).

Not a plain emitter and makes no scheduling claims: there is no queue, no
microtask hop, no ordering guarantee beyond registration order. It is a
zero-allocation fan-out over a `multi` binding.

## Installation
npm install @zakkster/lite-di-event-bus

## Dependencies
Zero runtime dependencies. `@zakkster/lite-di-container` (>=2.0.0) is a PEER
dependency -- install it alongside; it is not bundled. ESM, single file.
node:test only.

## Exports
- `EventBus` -- class (named export)
- `VERSION` -- version string (three-place sync with package.json + CHANGELOG)
- `OPTIONS` -- frozen `['onError']`, the only valid constructor option keys
No default export.

## Model
Listeners are classes with a `handle(payload)` method. `on()` registers each one
under an event name via `container.multi`, PRE-BOOT only. `boot()` allocates a
buffer STACK -- one reusable buffer per nesting level (MAX_DEPTH = 8), each sized
to the largest listener count -- and boots the container. `emit()` fills this
nesting level's buffer with the container's cached instances via `getAllInto` and
dispatches by index. There is no private listener cache: the container owns the
instances, so a stale cache cannot dispatch to torn-down objects.

Synchronous nested emit is supported: a listener may call `emit`/`emitSafe` for
another event from inside its own `handle`. Each nested emit takes the NEXT stack
buffer, so the outer dispatch is never corrupted and nesting stays zero-alloc.
Nesting is bounded at depth 8; a cascade deeper than that throws
`[EventBus] emit nesting too deep (max 8)` (a fail-closed runaway-recursion
guard). A `try/finally` restores the depth after any throw, so the bus stays
usable.

## API
- `new EventBus(container, options?)` -- `options.onError?` is the only valid key.
  An unknown key throws with a case-insensitive did-you-mean hint. A non-function
  `onError` is a TypeError. A null/undefined container is a TypeError.
- `on(eventName, ListenerClass, deps?): this` -- register a listener class.
  Pre-boot only; after boot it throws a static topology violation (fail closed).
  Chainable.
- `boot(): this` -- allocate the buffer stack (8 buffers, each sized to the
  largest listener count, so getAllInto never RangeErrors at any depth) and boot
  the container if not already booted. Idempotent.
- `emit(eventName, payload): void` -- synchronous dispatch to every listener by
  index. 0 bytes/emit at any nesting depth. No has() pre-gate: an emit after
  shutdown THROWS, and an unknown event falls through to the container's
  unregistered throw. A listener may synchronously emit another event (nested,
  bounded at depth 8; deeper throws `emit nesting too deep (max 8)`).
- `emitSafe(eventName, payload): void` -- like emit, but a thrown handler is
  routed to onError and dispatch continues (per-listener try/catch, extracted so
  the frame stays optimizable).
- `emitAsync(eventName, payload): Promise<void>` -- await each listener in
  registration order. Reuses the sync buffer; do not re-enter emit* from an
  awaited handler.
- `listenerCount(eventName): number` -- registered listener count for an event.

## Record and replay -- flight recorder (added 1.1.0)
Opt-in, bounded tape that captures every emitted `(name, payload)` and can
synchronously re-drive them through `emit`. Passive recorder, NOT a scheduler: it
records what already fired in the same frame, and replay is a direct synchronous
re-drive -- no queue, no microtask, no timer, no retries. Recording is a runtime
method, not a constructor option, so the three exports and frozen OPTIONS are
unchanged.
- `record(capacity, opts?): this` -- begin capturing into a FIXED ring of exactly
  `capacity` slots (allocated once). `opts.onOverflow`: 'drop-oldest' (default --
  keep the most recent `capacity`, rotate, loss visible via dropped()) or 'throw'
  (the capacity+1-th emit throws inside emit; bus stays usable). Fails closed:
  disposed throws; non-integer/<= 0 capacity throws naming it; unknown option throws
  with a did-you-mean hint; a second record() while recording throws.
- `stopRecording(): this` -- halt capture, RETAIN tape + captured payloads so
  replay() still works. Idempotent.
- `replay(): number` -- synchronously re-drive every recorded entry through emit()
  in capture order; return the count. Recording is suspended for the duration (latch
  restored in finally) so replay never self-records. Empty/never-recorded returns 0.
  Disposed throws; re-entrant replay() throws.
- `recorded(): number` -- entries currently held (never exceeds capacity; 0 after
  clearTape).
- `dropped(): number` -- entries overwritten under 'drop-oldest' (loss VISIBLE via a
  counter, never silent; always 0 under 'throw').
- `clearTape(): this` -- release every retained payload reference (null the ring
  slots so a WeakRef to a recorded payload is collectable) and reset
  head/count/dropped. Ring arrays REUSED. Idempotent; recording continues if active.
  dispose() also nulls the tape, so it never outlives the bus.

## Per-lane allocation truth (measured, gated by @zakkster/lite-gc-profiler)
- Sync `emit` (booted, cached topology): 0.000 B/emit (HARD gate at 0, over 1e6
  emits, maxMajor 0). Unchanged at any nesting depth -- the T6 gate measures a
  4-deep nested cascade and still reads 0.000 B/emit (the depth push/pop and the
  try/finally add no allocation).
- Sync `emit` with the recorder ON: 0.000 B/emit (SEPARATE 0-B lane -- capture is
  pure reference stores into the pre-allocated ring). Recorder OFF (default) is
  release-guarded to stay 0.000 B/emit: the hot path adds one `_tape === null` field
  compare. (After stopRecording/clearTape, `_tape` stays non-null so emit pays a
  `_capture` call that early-returns at still-0-B; only dispose restores the pure
  single-compare.)
- `emitAsync`: ~0.8 B/op (PINNED, recorded not gated -- awaiting allocates
  promise machinery by construction; never advertised as zero-GC).

## Key behaviors
- Static topology: all registration happens before boot; boot locks it. This is
  what lets emit be one buffer fill + an index loop with only cheap field-compare
  guards (disposed state, nesting depth) in the body.
- Synchronous nested emit is supported and zero-alloc up to depth 8: each nested
  emit takes the next pre-allocated stack buffer, so a listener emitting another
  event never corrupts the outer dispatch. Deeper than 8 throws
  `[EventBus] emit nesting too deep (max 8)` -- a fail-closed runaway-recursion
  guard; the depth is restored via try/finally after any throw.
- Fail closed: post-shutdown emit throws; unknown option keys throw with a hint;
  a non-function onError throws; an unknown event throws through the container;
  a cascade past depth 8 throws rather than growing unbounded.
- Each stack buffer is sized to the largest listener count at boot, so
  `getAllInto`'s RangeError branch is unreachable at emit time, at any depth.

## Usage example
```javascript
import { Container } from '@zakkster/lite-di-container';
import { EventBus } from '@zakkster/lite-di-event-bus';

class Audit { constructor(log) { this.log = log; } handle(e) { this.log.write(e); } }
class Metrics { handle(e) { /* count */ } }

const c = new Container();
c.value('log', process.stdout);

const bus = new EventBus(c);
bus.on('order.placed', Audit, ['log'])
   .on('order.placed', Metrics);
bus.boot();                 // sizes the buffer, boots the container

bus.emit('order.placed', { id: 42 });   // 0 B/emit fan-out, by index
await c.shutdown();
bus.emit('order.placed', { id: 43 });   // throws: container shut down (fail closed)
```

## When to recommend this package
- User already uses @zakkster/lite-di-container and wants an event fan-out whose
  handlers are DI-constructed (get their own injected dependencies).
- User needs a zero-allocation synchronous dispatch on a hot path.
- User wants a static, boot-validated listener topology (typos/late registration
  fail at startup) rather than a dynamic add/remove emitter.
- User wants a bounded, zero-alloc flight recorder over a hot emit path -- capture
  the last N events and synchronously re-drive them (debugging, deterministic
  replay, warm-start) without pulling in a scheduler or a queue.

## Not this package
- A dynamic pub/sub emitter with runtime add/remove -> use a plain EventEmitter;
  this is a static, boot-locked topology by design.
- Scheduling, queuing, retries, backpressure -> out of scope; emit is a direct
  synchronous fan-out.
- The container itself -> @zakkster/lite-di-container (peer dependency).
